title: Corryhabbie Hills Circuit
listingBlurb: Broad moorland above Glenfiddich — track help, heathery nonsense, Option A for shape, Option B for the laugh.
summary: Suggested route only. Broad moorland day above Glenfiddich with enough track help to keep it sensible and enough heathery nonsense to stop it feeling too tidy. Option A is the better actual route. Option B is probably the better laugh if the plan is just to get out, have a wander, stop for a puff, and not get precious about collecting every last bump.

disclaimerSection.title: Suggested route only
disclaimerSection.body: Built from map screenshots, anchor grid refs, and a best-effort read of the ground. It is not gospel, not a surveyed line, and not a substitute for using your own judgement on the hill. If the ground, weather, legs, or general mood says do something simpler, do something simpler.

weatherNote.title: Weather note
weatherNote.body: Dufftown-side forecast is looking more grey than glorious: cloudy through the morning and early afternoon, around 4°C early doors rising to about 12°C later on, with just a stray early shower showing.
weatherNote.supporting: Fine for a moorland stomp, just don’t expect cinematic golden-hour miracles.
weatherNote.disclaimerLabel: Short-term planning note, not a mountain-specific guarantee.

whyThisRoute.title: Why this route?
whyThisRoute.body: This hill group makes most sense when you treat it as a broad moorland circuit with options, not a rigid “must touch every contour bump” exercise. The western side gives you the bigger sweep of tops; Corryhabbie gives you the cleaner-feeling high point; and the track options on the return stop the last chunk turning into needless nonsense.
callouts: Option A is the better actual route.
Option B is probably the better laugh.
whyThisRoute.supporting: Both are valid. One is just a bit more “proper day out,” and the other is a bit more “let’s get up there, have a laugh, and not get weirdly precious about every lump on the map.”

recommendationBlock.title: Our honest take
lines: Option A is the better actual route.
Option B is probably the better laugh.
recommendationBlock.supporting: If the weather’s fine and everyone’s up for a proper moorland stomp, go Option A. If the day is more about getting out, stopping for a puff, and not turning it into a forced march, go Option B.

qualityMeter.headline: Decent chance of a good yin
qualityMeter.verdict: Broad open hill, decent route options, and very workable weather — but enough bog/heather tax and flat-light risk to stop it being an automatic classic.

factors.label: Flexible route choice
factors.note: Two good route options means you can trim the nonsense if needed.

factors.label: Weather is usable
factors.note: Grey but workable usually beats dramatic but miserable.

factors.label: Broad moorland ground
factors.note: Big open hill gives freedom, but can feel a bit featureless in flat light.

factors.label: Bog / heather tax
factors.note: Could be pure shite in places if the ground is holding water.

factors.label: Social-day potential
factors.note: Good kind of hill for a relaxed late start and a few sit-down stops.

subscores.label: Views potential
subscores.note: Big open hill and broad moorland positions should still give decent atmosphere, even if the light's not doing anything special.

subscores.label: Ground quality
subscores.note: This is where the day can get a bit suspect. Plenty of scope for bog/heather tax and false optimism.

subscores.label: General craic factor
subscores.note: Late-start, social, broad hill, flexible route choices, good wee puff spots — hard not to get something out of it.

parkingNote: Start at the parker around NJ 27613 30622 near Ellivreid. Park considerately — don’t block gates, farm access, or anything that might need a tractor later.
anchorRefsIntro: These are there to help shape the day, not to pretend you’re following a perfect engineered line.

routeOptions.name: Option A — Full round
routeOptions.reason: The one with proper circuit energy — awkward west done early, cleaner finish later.
routeOptions.lineDescription: Start near Ellivreid, get Hill of Achmore out the way first, then sweep across Càrn a’ Bhodaich, Cairn Dregnie, Carn an t-Suidhe, curve back through the broad ridge ground toward Muckle Lapprach, then finish the main business on Corryhabbie Hill before using the tidier return lines back out.
routeOptions.whyPick: Because it feels like a real circuit rather than a quick tag-and-bail. If the weather’s behaving and everyone’s in decent form, this is the one that makes the most sense.
routeOptions.tradeoff: A bit more heathery linking, a bit more bog lottery, and a bit more commitment. Fine if the vibe is “proper day out,” less ideal if everyone’s half-cooked before you’ve even left the car.

routeOptions.name: Option B — Looser / easier day
routeOptions.reason: Best bits without hoovering up every lump — easy enough to trim if everyone’s half-cooked.
routeOptions.lineDescription: Start near Ellivreid, take Hill of Achmore, head up for Muckle Lapprach, carry on to Corryhabbie Hill, and then either call that good enough or tack on an extra bit if everyone still fancies it.
routeOptions.whyPick: Because it gives you the best bits without hoovering up every lump on the map. Easier to shorten, easier to chat your way through, easier to bail out of if conditions or enthusiasm dip.
routeOptions.tradeoff: It doesn’t feel as “complete” as the full round. If you like the satisfaction of a cleaner circuit, this is the slightly lazier version. Which, to be fair, may be exactly the point.

goodStopsDetail.intro: Good wee spots to stop for a puff / regroup.

spots.title: Corryhabbie Hill
spots.description: Biggest-feeling perch of the lot. If you’re going to stop and stare at the world for five minutes, this is the obvious one.

spots.title: Muckle Lapprach shoulder
spots.description: Good sit-down spot without feeling like you’ve dropped too low or wandered off the day.

spots.title: Track junction near NJ 28983 28035
spots.description: Useful regroup point if folk want to decide whether they’re still keen, still mobile, or just pretending they know where the clean finish is.

whatDayFeelsLike.title: What this day probably feels like
whatDayFeelsLike.body: Broad open hill. No real technical drama. Plenty of space to make your own decisions. Enough track help to keep it civilised, enough peat and heather to remind you you’re still in Scotland.
whatDayFeelsLike.supporting: At its best, this is the sort of day where you’re just moving through big open ground, stopping where it looks good, and not overthinking it. At its worst, it’s a lot of “that bit looked drier from over there” followed by a wet foot and a bit of swearing.
summaryLines: could be boggy nonsense in places
still a decent social hill day

terrainDetail.title: Terrain & vibe
terrainDetail.body: Expect broad open hill, heathery ground, and a decent chance of at least some boggy nonsense. Nothing especially technical, just the usual question of how much shite you want to voluntarily add to your own day.
terrainDetail.supporting: The better bits should feel open and easy-going. The worse bits will probably be the classic Scottish upland combo of peat, tufty grass, and false confidence. There’s enough track help in the wider area to keep the day sensible though, which is why this hill group works well for a relaxed team day rather than a hyper-serious mission.

wildlifeIntro: Closer look at what you’re sharing the hill with — and what the ground’s trying to tell you.

wildlifeCards.title: Red grouse
wildlifeCards.body: Very on-brand for this sort of heather moorland. If you see one explode out the heather and nearly take your head off, that’s about right.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Tells you you’re in proper moorland country.

wildlifeCards.title: Meadow pipit
wildlifeCards.body: Small, brown, streaky, and easy to miss until one flutters up and gives itself away.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: One of the most likely birds you’ll actually notice if you’re paying attention.

wildlifeCards.title: Red deer
wildlifeCards.body: Always a realistic shout in Scottish upland country if you actually look up once in a while.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Makes the whole place feel bigger and a bit wilder when you spot one.

wildlifeCards.title: Heather / blaeberry / bog moss / cottongrass
wildlifeCards.body: This is the proper texture of the hill. Lovely to look at, and sometimes a decent clue that the next few metres deserve suspicion.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Helps you read the ground and explains why some bits feel great and some bits feel like a trap.

lookoutGalleryIntro: Red grouse if the heather’s lively, meadow pipits doing their wee fluttery thing, and maybe red deer if you’re actually looking up now and then. On the ground, it’s all heather, blaeberry, peaty bits and cottongrass in the wetter hollows — which is lovely until your foot goes through it.

lookoutGallery.title: Broad moorland ridge
lookoutGallery.caption: Cairn beside Morton's Way on Corryhabbie — big open ground, Ben Rinnes across the glen, and that ‘proper hill day’ sweep.

lookoutGallery.title: Heather and blaeberry ground
lookoutGallery.caption: Open moor on Corryhabbie itself — the heathery, peaty texture you’re signing up for, just with more sky than your boots will thank you for.

lookoutGallery.title: Cottongrass / bog indicator
lookoutGallery.caption: Same fluffy bog clue you get in wet hollows here — this one’s Hermaness on Unst, not Corryhabbie, but the ‘aye, that’s soft’ energy is identical.

lookoutGallery.title: Red grouse

planningFooterNote: For planning only — check weather, ground, access, and your own willingness to tolerate boggy nonsense on the day.
